entries.title: Overview of the Gastrointestinal Tract

testable_competencies.gi_anatomy_overview: Recognize basic GI tract anatomy/physiology as background for the disease-specific units that follow.

entries.zero_question_reason: Normal anatomy/physiology background; not independently testable but frames later disease units.

entries.title: Visualizing the Gastrointestinal Tract (Imaging and Endoscopy Overview)

testable_competencies.gi_imaging_overview: Recognize the range of imaging/endoscopic modalities used to investigate GI disease (used to select investigations within specific disease units).

entries.zero_question_reason: Modality overview; overlaps with Medical Imaging chapter and is not independently testable outside disease-specific investigation choices already covered per-unit.

entries.title: Differential Diagnosis of Common GI Complaints

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 3-2's own key/enabling objectives require constructing a differential for acute abdominal pain; this unit is the chapter's index/framework for that differential.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Same reasoning for chronic abdominal pain.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Framework underlies determining likely cause of upper GI bleeding.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Framework underlies determining likely cause of lower GI bleeding.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Framework underlies the acute-diarrhea differential.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Framework underlies the jaundice differential.

testable_competencies.gi_ddx_framework: Construct a differential diagnosis for common GI presentations (abdominal pain, GI bleeding, diarrhea, jaundice, dysphagia, constipation) using a structured approach.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 3-2's causal-conditions list for acute abdominal pain explicitly names 'Gastroesophageal reflux disease' as an upper-abdominal-region cause.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 14's causal-conditions list for chest pain names 'Esophageal spasm or esophagitis' as a noncardiac cause requiring differentiation from cardiac chest pain.

testable_competencies.gerd_recognition: Diagnose GERD and initiate an appropriate initial management plan (lifestyle, acid suppression), and recognize when to investigate for alarm features/complications.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Complication of GERD, which is explicitly named in objective 3-2's causal-conditions list; no dedicated MCC objective for Barrett's surveillance protocols specifically.

testable_competencies.barretts_recognition: Recognize Barrett's esophagus as a complication of chronic GERD requiring endoscopic surveillance given esophageal adenocarcinoma risk.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 26 is titled 'Dysphagia' with key objective text identical to this study unit's core competency ('differentiate oropharyngeal from esophageal causes').

testable_competencies.dysphagia_approach: Differentiate oropharyngeal from esophageal dysphagia and initiate a management plan based on cause and severity.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 26's causal-conditions list explicitly names 'diffuse esophageal spasm' and 'scleroderma, achalasia' under esophageal neuromuscular dysphagia.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 14's causal-conditions list names 'esophageal spasm' as a noncardiac chest-pain cause.

testable_competencies.motor_disorder_recognition: Recognize achalasia and diffuse esophageal spasm as neuromuscular causes of esophageal dysphagia and select appropriate initial investigation (e.g., manometry, barium swallow).

entries.title: Structural Esophageal Narrowing (Diverticula, Peptic Stricture, Webs and Rings)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 26's causal-conditions list explicitly names 'Zenker diverticulum', 'lower esophageal ring, web', and 'peptic stricture' as structural/mechanical dysphagia causes.

testable_competencies.structural_narrowing_recognition: Recognize Zenker diverticulum, peptic stricture, and esophageal webs/rings as structural causes of intermittent or progressive dysphagia.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 26's causal-conditions list explicitly names 'tumour' under progressive esophageal dysphagia.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 118-2's causal-conditions list explicitly names 'esophageal cancer' as a medical-disease cause of weight loss.

testable_competencies.esophageal_ca_recognition: Recognize progressive dysphagia and other alarm features (weight loss, odynophagia) as suggestive of esophageal carcinoma and initiate urgent endoscopic investigation.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Falls under objective 26's esophageal-dysphagia/odynophagia scope; no dedicated MCC objective for infectious esophagitis specifically.

testable_competencies.infectious_esophagitis_recognition: Recognize odynophagia in an immunocompromised patient as suggestive of infectious esophagitis (candida, HSV, CMV) and initiate appropriate investigation/treatment.

entries.title: Stomach and Duodenum Overview

testable_competencies.stomach_physiology: Recognize basic gastric anatomy/physiology (acid secretion, mucosal defense) as background for peptic disease units.

entries.zero_question_reason: Normal anatomy/physiology background framing the disease-specific units that follow.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 3-3's causal-conditions list for chronic abdominal pain explicitly names 'Ulcer and nonulcer dyspepsia'.

testable_competencies.dyspepsia_approach: Differentiate ulcer from non-ulcer (functional) dyspepsia, identify alarm features requiring endoscopy, and initiate an empiric or test-and-treat management plan.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 6-1's causal-conditions list for upper GI bleeding explicitly names 'Gastritis'.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 3-2's causal-conditions list names 'Peptic ulcer disease, gastritis' together as an upper-abdominal acute-pain cause.

testable_competencies.gastritis_recognition: Recognize gastritis as a cause of upper abdominal pain and/or upper GI bleeding and identify common etiologies (H. pylori, NSAIDs, alcohol).

entries.title: Peptic Ulcer Disease (H. pylori, NSAID-, and Stress-Induced)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 6-1's causal-conditions list explicitly names 'Peptic ulcer disease' as an ulcerative/erosive cause of upper GI bleeding.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 3-2's causal-conditions list names 'Peptic ulcer disease, gastritis' as an upper-abdominal acute-pain cause.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 14's causal-conditions list names 'Peptic ulcer disease' as a noncardiac chest-pain cause.

testable_competencies.pud_diagnosis: Diagnose peptic ulcer disease, determine H. pylori vs. NSAID vs. stress-related etiology, and initiate an appropriate management plan including H. pylori eradication and PPI prophylaxis where indicated.
testable_competencies.pud_complications: Recognize complications of PUD, including hemorrhage and perforation, as causes of acute abdominal pain and upper GI bleeding.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 3-3's causal-conditions list for chronic abdominal pain explicitly names 'Malignancy' in the upper-abdominal-region category.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 6-1's causal-conditions list names 'Tumors' as an upper GI bleeding cause.

testable_competencies.gastric_ca_recognition: Recognize alarm features (weight loss, early satiety, persistent dyspepsia, GI bleeding) suggestive of gastric carcinoma and initiate urgent endoscopic investigation.

entries.title: Classification of Diarrhea

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: This classification framework is the organizing structure of objective 22-2's own causal-conditions list (luminal/mucosal/motility categories).

testable_competencies.diarrhea_classification: Apply the osmotic/secretory/inflammatory/motility classification framework to localize a cause of diarrhea.

entries.zero_question_reason: Organizing framework for objective 22-2's own causal-conditions categories, not an independently testable competency separate from the Acute/Chronic Diarrhea units it frames.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 22-1 is titled 'Acute diarrhea' with matching key objective text; its causal-conditions list includes infection (viruses, bacteria, parasites), which covers traveller's diarrhea.

testable_competencies.acute_diarrhea_diagnosis: Diagnose the cause, severity, and complications of acute diarrhea (lasting <1 week), with particular attention to risk factors for specific causes (including travel) and assessment for dehydration/electrolyte complications.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 22-2 is titled 'Chronic diarrhea' with matching key objective text.

testable_competencies.chronic_diarrhea_diagnosis: Diagnose the cause, severity, and complications of chronic diarrhea, contrasting small vs. large bowel causes.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 22-2's causal-conditions list explicitly enumerates 'Steatorrhea', 'Pancreatic insufficiency', 'Bacterial overgrowth', and 'Lactase deficiency' under luminal/mucosal causes of chronic diarrhea.

testable_competencies.malabsorption_recognition: Recognize steatorrhea/malabsorption (pancreatic insufficiency, bacterial overgrowth, mucosal disease) as a cause of chronic diarrhea and select appropriate initial investigations.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 22-2's causal-conditions list explicitly names 'Celiac disease' under mucosal causes of chronic diarrhea.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 52's causal-conditions list explicitly names 'celiac disease' as a cause of abnormal liver function tests.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 3-3's causal-conditions list explicitly names 'Food allergies and intolerances (including celiac disease)'.

testable_competencies.celiac_diagnosis: Diagnose celiac disease via serology and duodenal biopsy in a patient with chronic diarrhea, malabsorption, iron-deficiency anemia, or abnormal liver enzymes, and initiate gluten-free diet management.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 3-3's causal-conditions list explicitly names 'Inflammatory bowel disease' under lower-abdominal bowel disease.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 22-2's causal-conditions list explicitly names 'Inflammatory bowel disease' under inflammatory chronic diarrhea.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 3-2's causal-conditions list explicitly names 'Inflammatory bowel disease' under lower-abdominal acute-pain causes.

testable_competencies.ibd_general_approach: Recognize IBD as a cause of chronic abdominal pain and/or diarrhea, including extraintestinal manifestations, and initiate an appropriate diagnostic workup.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Crohn's disease is the named transmural IBD subtype captured under objective 3-3's explicit 'Inflammatory bowel disease' causal condition.

testable_competencies.crohns_recognition: Recognize the distinguishing features of Crohn's disease (skip lesions, transmural inflammation, any GI segment, fistulizing/stricturing complications) and initiate an appropriate diagnostic/management plan.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 6-2's causal-conditions list explicitly names 'ulcerative colitis' as an inflammatory cause of lower GI bleeding.

testable_competencies.uc_recognition: Recognize the distinguishing features of ulcerative colitis (continuous colonic/rectal involvement, mucosal inflammation, bloody diarrhea) and initiate an appropriate diagnostic/management plan.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 3-3's causal-conditions list explicitly names 'Irritable bowel syndrome' under lower-abdominal bowel disease.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 16-1's causal-conditions list for adult constipation explicitly names 'Irritable bowel syndrome'.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 1's causal-conditions list for abdominal distension explicitly names 'Irritable bowel syndrome'.

testable_competencies.ibs_diagnosis: Diagnose IBS as a functional motility disorder using symptom-based criteria after excluding organic disease, in a patient with chronic abdominal pain, altered bowel habits, or constipation.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 16-1 is titled 'Adult constipation' with matching key objective text.

testable_competencies.constipation_diagnosis: Diagnose the cause and severity of adult constipation and initiate an appropriate management plan.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 6-1 is titled 'Upper gastrointestinal bleeding' with matching key objective text; its causal-conditions list explicitly names 'Trauma (e.g., Mallory-Weiss tear)'.

testable_competencies.ugib_management: Diagnose the cause, severity, and complications of hematemesis or melena; determine and manage hemodynamic status and resuscitate as needed.
testable_competencies.mallory_weiss_recognition: Recognize Mallory-Weiss tear (post-retching mucosal laceration) as a traumatic cause of upper GI bleeding.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 6-1's causal-conditions list explicitly names 'Portal hypertension' as an upper GI bleeding cause.

testable_competencies.variceal_bleed_management: Recognize esophageal varices secondary to portal hypertension as a high-risk cause of upper GI bleeding and initiate emergency resuscitation and hemorrhage-control measures.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 6-2 is titled 'Lower gastrointestinal bleeding' with matching key objective text; its causal-conditions list explicitly names 'diverticulosis' under vascular causes.

testable_competencies.lgib_management: Diagnose the cause, severity, and complications of lower GI bleeding, with attention to hemodynamic status and need for specialized care.
testable_competencies.diverticular_bleed_recognition: Recognize diverticulosis as the most common vascular cause of lower GI bleeding.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 6-2's causal-conditions list explicitly names 'infection' under inflammatory causes of lower GI bleeding.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 22-1's causal-conditions list explicitly names infection (viruses, bacteria, parasites) as a cause of acute diarrhea.

testable_competencies.infectious_colitis_recognition: Recognize infectious colitis (including C. difficile) as a cause of acute/bloody diarrhea and lower GI bleeding, and initiate appropriate testing and treatment.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 6-2's key/enabling objective text explicitly states the candidate 'will also identify patients who are at high risk for colorectal cancer for a screening program'; its causal-conditions list names 'polyp, carcinoma' under neoplastic causes.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 74's causal-conditions list for the middle-aged/older adult explicitly names 'Cancer screening (e.g., breast, colon, prostate, skin)'.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Iron-deficiency (microcytic) anemia is explicitly listed under objective 42-1 and is a classic occult presentation of colorectal carcinoma.

testable_competencies.crc_screening_and_diagnosis: Identify patients at high risk for colorectal cancer for a screening program, and diagnose colorectal carcinoma/polyps in a patient presenting with lower GI bleeding, iron-deficiency anemia, or a change in bowel habits.

entries.title: Familial Colorectal Cancer Syndromes

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: These syndromes are the paradigm case of objective 6-2's explicit requirement to 'identify patients who are at high risk for colorectal cancer for a screening program'; detailed genetic classification (Lynch/FAP subtypes) is kept at a recognition-level depth per Gastroenterology scope cautions against subspecialty genetics/pathology minutiae.

testable_competencies.hereditary_crc_recognition: Recognize features suggestive of a hereditary colorectal cancer syndrome (young age, family history pattern, polyp burden) warranting genetics referral and intensified screening.

do_not_test: Specific Lynch syndrome gene mutations (MLH1/MSH2/MSH6/PMS2) or detailed FAP genotype-phenotype correlations - specialist genetics detail.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 3-4's causal-conditions list explicitly names 'Fissures, fistulas' and 'Hemorrhoids' under anorectal disease.

testable_competencies.anorectal_disease_diagnosis: Diagnose the cause of anorectal pain (hemorrhoids, fissure, abscess, fistula) and initiate an appropriate management plan, remaining cognizant of red flags for underlying malignancy.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 52 is titled 'Abnormal liver function tests' with a key objective structured around the same hepatocellular/cholestatic diagnostic approach.

testable_competencies.lft_interpretation: Interpret a pattern of abnormal liver enzymes (hepatocellular vs. cholestatic) to guide further hepatobiliary investigation.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 49's causal-conditions list names 'Hepatocellular injury' as a jaundice cause, of which viral hepatitis is the classic example.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 52's causal-conditions list explicitly names 'infection' under both acute and chronic hepatocellular causes of abnormal LFTs.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 3-2's causal-conditions list explicitly names 'Acute hepatitis' under upper-abdominal acute-pain causes.

testable_competencies.viral_hepatitis_diagnosis: Diagnose acute or chronic viral hepatitis (A, B, C, D) using serology, differentiate transmission routes and chronicity risk, and recognize indications for antiviral treatment/screening.
testable_competencies.hbv_hcv_screening: Recognize indications for hepatitis B and C screening and the risk of chronic infection/cirrhosis/hepatocellular carcinoma.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Falls under objective 52's 'chronic hepatocellular' causal category; not individually enumerated in the objective's causal-conditions list, so mapped as COMPONENT rather than DIRECT.

testable_competencies.aih_recognition: Recognize autoimmune hepatitis as a cause of chronic hepatocellular liver disease, typically in a young woman with elevated autoantibodies, warranting immunosuppressive treatment.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 52's causal-conditions list explicitly names 'medication' under both acute and chronic hepatocellular causes of abnormal LFTs.

testable_competencies.dili_recognition: Recognize medication/toxin exposure (including acetaminophen overdose) as a cause of acute or chronic liver injury and initiate appropriate management (e.g., N-acetylcysteine for acetaminophen toxicity).

entries.title: Wilson's Disease

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 52's causal-conditions list does not enumerate Wilson's disease (only 'celiac disease' as an 'other' example); mapped as WEAK since no genetic/metabolic liver-disease category is explicitly named in the registry text.

testable_competencies.wilsons_recognition: Recognize Wilson's disease as a rare genetic/metabolic cause of liver disease with neuropsychiatric features (Kayser-Fleischer rings) in a young patient with unexplained liver disease.

entries.zero_question_reason: Rare genetic/metabolic disease with WEAK MCC evidence; kept in scope at recognition-level only per Gastroenterology scope cautions against subspecialty pathology detail.
entries.mcc_evidence_retention_reason: Retained at WEAK strength (rather than cleared to empty) to document that Wilson's disease was searched for and considered, not overlooked, despite SPECIALIST_DETAIL classification.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Falls under objective 52's chronic hepatocellular causal category; not individually enumerated in the registry text, so mapped as MODERATE rather than STRONG despite hemochromatosis being a common, high-yield diagnosis.

testable_competencies.hemochromatosis_recognition: Recognize hereditary hemochromatosis (elevated ferritin/transferrin saturation, classic triad) as a cause of liver disease and initiate iron-studies-based diagnosis.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Falls under objective 52's hepatocellular causal category (alcohol as a toxic/chronic hepatocellular insult).

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 103 ('Substance use or addictive disorders') explicitly requires identifying alcohol use and its consequences, of which alcohol-related liver disease is a major one.

testable_competencies.ald_recognition: Recognize the spectrum of alcohol-related liver disease (steatosis, alcoholic hepatitis, cirrhosis) and screen for/address the underlying alcohol use disorder.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Falls under objective 52's chronic hepatocellular causal category; not individually enumerated in the registry text, so mapped as MODERATE despite high prevalence/testability.

testable_competencies.masld_recognition: Recognize MASLD as the most common cause of chronic liver disease in patients with metabolic syndrome and its progression risk to steatohepatitis/cirrhosis.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Falls squarely under objective 52's 'acute hepatocellular' causal category (e.g., infection, medication).

testable_competencies.alf_recognition: Recognize acute liver failure (coagulopathy plus encephalopathy in a patient without prior liver disease) as a life-threatening emergency requiring urgent transplant-center referral.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 49's causal-conditions list explicitly names 'cirrhosis' under intrahepatic cholestasis causes of jaundice.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 1's causal-conditions list explicitly names 'portal hypertension' under transudative ascites causes of abdominal distension.

testable_competencies.cirrhosis_diagnosis: Diagnose cirrhosis and its complications (portal hypertension, variceal bleeding, ascites, hepatic encephalopathy, hepatocellular carcinoma) and initiate an appropriate management plan.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 2's causal-conditions list for abdominal masses explicitly names 'liver tumour' under gastrointestinal neoplasms.

testable_competencies.hcc_recognition: Recognize HCC as a complication of cirrhosis warranting surveillance (ultrasound +/- AFP) and identify features suggestive of HCC on imaging/labs.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 6-1's causal-conditions list explicitly names 'Portal hypertension' as an upper GI bleeding cause.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 1's causal-conditions list explicitly names 'portal hypertension' as a transudative-ascites cause of abdominal distension.

testable_competencies.portal_htn_recognition: Recognize portal hypertension as the mechanism underlying variceal bleeding and ascites in cirrhosis.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Falls under the complications of chronic hepatocellular liver disease captured generally by objective 52; not individually enumerated in the registry text.

testable_competencies.hepatic_encephalopathy_management: Recognize hepatic encephalopathy as a complication of cirrhosis/portal hypertension, identify precipitants (GI bleed, infection, constipation, medication non-adherence), and initiate treatment (e.g., lactulose).

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 1's causal-conditions list explicitly enumerates ascites with the exudative (low SAAG, e.g., peritoneal carcinomatosis) vs. transudative (high SAAG, e.g., portal hypertension) framework matching this unit's core competency.

testable_competencies.ascites_diagnosis: Diagnose the cause of ascites using the serum-ascites albumin gradient (transudative vs. exudative) and initiate appropriate management (e.g., sodium restriction, diuretics, paracentesis for SBP work-up).

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 49 is titled 'Jaundice' with matching key objective text; its causal-conditions list explicitly names 'Extrahepatic cholestasis (e.g., cholelithiasis)'.

testable_competencies.obstructive_jaundice_diagnosis: Diagnose the cause, severity, and complications of jaundice, with particular attention to identifying extrahepatic/obstructive (surgical) causes requiring urgent intervention.
